fact: Namibia's Chief Registrar said it is working to strengthen timely birth and death registration by monitoring notification and registration through its e-notification system.

A speaker at the Africa CDC learning visit said the e-birth notification system, introduced in 2017, has been implemented nationwide and connects 153 state and private facilities, per Home Affairs Minister Iipumbu's account.
Home Affairs Minister Iipumbu said the e-death notification, introduced in 2018, now operates in 153 state and private facilities.
A speaker at the Africa CDC learning visit said Namibia records birth registration coverage of close to 99%, in March 2026.
The Ministry of Home Affairs says 126 state and private hospitals are now equipped with the electronic birth notification system that lets nurses record births instantly into the national system.

The Ministry of Home Affairs with UNDP tested a mobile ID prototype at Otjimbingwe, Erongo, letting a mother and community health worker submit and digitally sign birth registration data by phone, with rollout planned for 2026 after nationwide consultations.

The Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security says its e-birth notification system, which electronically notifies the e-NPRS of births, was implemented at 22 named hospitals and health centres in 2019/2020.
The Ministry says its e-death notification system, electronic notification of deaths in line with births, was implemented at 26 named sites in 2019/2020.

The Namibia Statistics Agency says births are notified electronically from health facilities (e-birth notification launched 2017) and captured on the National Population Register System, but some registration offices lack computers and connectivity and transfer paper records to head office.
The Namibia Statistics Agency says the e-death notification system was launched in 2018 and deaths are captured on the National Population Register System, with 2021 death completeness at 97.6%.
The Namibia Statistics Agency reports birth registration completeness of 99.2% in 2018 falling to 62.0% in 2021 (under-five completeness 19.9%), a national rate not tied to the digital system.
The World Bank's WDI lists completeness of birth registration in Namibia at 78.1% for 2016, a national rate not tied to a digital system.
